decisions.reason: Connects the bare top-level import in lib/client.js to the boot-assembled classic-script combo whose single compile failure (position 1:1) stops all entry registration; explains dsh-typert-registry is merely the first awaited innocent entry, and scopes the invalidity to classic-script contexts rather than claiming ESM is invalid everywhere.

Bisects the patch-layer insert rows and parses bundles under classic-script goal (.cjs copy), explicitly noting plain node --check auto-detects ESM and is insufficient; describes the window.__ModuleLoader__.load({id, factory}) wrapper, package-name identity, require('react') inside the factory, and the factory returning module.exports with apply and inject exports.

Uses plugin-apply-error.txt and the bare registration with kind/scope to explain another entry owns the declaration and apply order is undefined; shows the exact ctx.slots.inject('settings.section', () => ctx.slots.register(...)) wrapping, lists registrant fields name/id/order (label) and excludes declaration-owned kind/scope.

Explains the combo is assembled once per boot so edits and refresh do not rebuild it; requires full host stop/restart per iteration, tree-kill of an orphaned Windows process holding the port (taskkill /PID /T /F), then refresh and plugin-list verification; explains EADDRINUSE as the old process retaining the port, not a packaging defect.

Proposes per-module classic-script validation and true culprit attribution at assembly/import isolation instead of blaming the first awaited entry, plus a concrete authoring checklist covering the loader factory, host React via require, inject/apply, deferred cross-entry slots, restart and Windows tree cleanup — well beyond a generic 'add tests'.

caps.reason: Final advice prescribes the loader wrapper, slots.inject deferred registration without kind/scope, and full host restarts; none of the listed contradictions is affirmatively recommended.
